job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let us look at decimals. Rahul, if you add 5 and 0.3, what do you get? Rahul: I think it is 0.8 because I just line up the digits. Teacher: Not quite. Remember, 5 is the same as 5.0. When adding, you must align the decimal points, not the last digits. Priya, how about comparing 0.8 and 0.83? Priya: I think 0.8 is larger because it has fewer digits. Teacher: That is a common mistake. Think of them as fractions: 0.8 is 80/100 and 0.83 is 83/100. Since 83 is more than 80, 0.83 is actually greater. Rahul: What about 0.4 and 0.40? Are they different? Teacher: No, they are equal. Adding a zero at the end does not change the value. Finally, remember that the first place after the decimal is the tenths place, which is larger than the hundredths place. If you have 0.5, that is five tenths, while 0.05 is five hundredths. Priya: So, 0.5 is definitely larger than 0.05? Teacher: Exactly. Always look at the place value of the digits rather than just counting how many digits are written. By lining up the decimal points and comparing place values, you will never be confused again.

items.evidence: When adding, you must align the decimal points, not the last digits.
items.q: Meena adds 5 and 0.3 by lining up the decimal points. What answer does she get?
items.explain: 5 is 5.0, so aligning decimal points gives 5.0 + 0.3 = 5.3.

wrong.why: lines up last digits, treating 5 like 0.5
puts the 3 in the wrong place when aligning
